strings.name: Abhijit Banerjee
strings.role: Economist · Development and poverty policy researcher
strings.summary: Abhijit Banerjee studies information, poverty and development policy, focusing on specific problems and testable interventions. With Esther Duflo and Sendhil Mullainathan, he co-founded J-PAL to apply randomized evaluation to education, health and financial services and connect evidence with policy institutions. He shared the 2019 economics prize with Duflo and Michael Kremer, explained research to wider audiences through books including Poor Economics, and joined the University of Zurich in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach the effective July 2026 Zurich appointment, with an October 2026 CV also checked. MIT and J-PAL ties are retained; local trial results are not presented as guarantees for every society.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped develop experimental development economics, influencing public policy through research on poverty, education and health.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace and upbringing
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Born in Mumbai, India; raised in Kolkata
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BSc, University of Calcutta (1981); MA, Jawaharlal Nehru University (1983); PhD, Harvard University (1988)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Advancing experimental development economics
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Shared the 2019 economics prize with Duflo and Kremer for an experimental approach to alleviating poverty.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Connecting research and policy
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Co-founded J-PAL and explored education, health and household decisions in books including Poor Economics.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Joins the University of Zurich
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Became Lemann Foundation Professor in Economics, continuing work on development, education and public policy with Duflo.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes Good Economics for Hard Times
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Co-authored a public-facing book with Duflo on immigration, trade, growth and other questions in evidence-based policy.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Shares the economics prize
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Received the prize with Duflo and Kremer, bringing experimental poverty research to a wider audience.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Poor Economics
strings.timeline.event-04.text: With Duflo, used field research to explain decisions made by people in poverty and evidence on different policies.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Co-founds J-PAL
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Founded the Poverty Action Lab with Duflo and Sendhil Mullainathan to support randomized policy evaluation.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Joins MIT
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Joined MIT after teaching at Princeton and Harvard, continuing research in development economics and information.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Earns a Harvard doctorate
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Completed a dissertation on information economics and began teaching at Princeton University.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes his master’s degree at JNU
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Earned a master’s degree in New Delhi before pursuing doctoral study at Harvard.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Graduates from the University of Calcutta
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Completed undergraduate economics studies before further research training in India and the United States.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Mumbai
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Mumbai and raised in Kolkata, later making poverty and development central research topics.
